```{r include = FALSE}

# note: unstandardized questionnaire data ('us' stands for 'unstandardized')
questionnaire_us_study1 <- read.csv("../Data/questionnaire_us_study1.csv")
questionnaire_us_study2 <- read.csv("../Data/questionnaire_us_study2.csv")

# note: hr stands for 'horizon', referring to the Horizon task
hr_long_study1 <- read.csv("../Data/hr_long_study1.csv") # behavioral data in long format
hr_wide_study1 <- read.csv("../Data/hr_wide_study1.csv") # behavioral data in wide format

hr_long_study2 <- read.csv("../Data/hr_long_study2.csv") # behavioral data in long format
hr_wide_study2 <- read.csv("../Data/hr_wide_study2.csv") # behavioral data in wide format

# note: tr stands for 'tree', referring to the Orchard task
tr_long <- read.csv("../Data/tr_long.csv")
tr_wide <- read.csv("../Data/tr_wide.csv")

```

# Descriptive statistics 
### Horizon task (**main text table 2**)
```{r}
# Study 1
hr_wide_study1 %>% select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% st(.)

# Study 2
hr_wide_study2 %>% select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% st(.)

# t-test
hr_study1 <- hr_wide_study1 %>% 
  select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% 
  mutate(study = "Primary")
hr_study2 <- hr_wide_study2 %>% 
  select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% 
  mutate(study = "Replication")
hr <- rbind(hr_study1,hr_study2)

a <- nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "directed_exploration", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
b <- nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "strategic_exploration", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
c <- nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "rt_5thchoice", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
d <- nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "reward_maximization", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
e <- nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "mean_reward", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 

bind_rows(a, b, c, d, e)
```

### Questionnaires (**main text table 3**)
```{r}
# Study 1
questionnaire_us_study1 %>% select(unpredictability,family_income,digit_span) %>% st(.)

# Study 2
questionnaire_us_study2 %>% select(unpredictability,family_income,digit_span) %>% st(.)

# t-test
q_study1 <- questionnaire_us_study1 %>% select(unpredictability,family_income,digit_span) %>% mutate(study = "Primary")
q_study2 <- questionnaire_us_study2 %>% select(unpredictability,family_income,digit_span) %>% mutate(study = "Replication")
q <- rbind(q_study1,q_study2)

a <- nice_t_test(data = q, response = "unpredictability", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
b <- nice_t_test(data = q, response = "family_income", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
c <- nice_t_test(data = q, response = "digit_span", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 

bind_rows(a, b, c)
```

### Orchard task (**main text results**)
```{r}
a <- nice_t_test(data = tr_wide, response = "threshold_short",mu = 0, warning = FALSE)
b <- nice_t_test(data = tr_wide, response = "threshold_short",mu = 0, warning = FALSE)
```

# Baseline evidence of exploration under task manipulation
### Horizon task (**main text table 1**)
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rownames <- c("average directed exploration (1-sample t-test)", 
              "directed exploration in H1 games (1-sample t-test)", 
              "directed exploration in H6 games (1-sample t-test)",
              "strategic directed exploration (2-sample t-test between H1 and H6 games)")

# Study 1
df_baseline_study1 <- hr_long_study1 %>% group_by(id, game_length) %>% summarise(avg_explore = mean(chose_high_info_value))

a <- nice_t_test(data = df_baseline_study1, response = "avg_explore",mu = 0, warning = FALSE)
b <- nice_t_test(data = subset(df_baseline_study1, game_length == 5), response = "avg_explore",mu = 0, warning = FALSE) 
c <- nice_t_test(data = subset(df_baseline_study1, game_length == 10), response = "avg_explore",mu = 0, warning = FALSE)
d <- nice_t_test(data = df_baseline_study1, response = "avg_explore", group = "game_length", alternative = "less", var.equal = TRUE) 

bind_rows(a, b, c, d) %>% cbind(rownames) %>% select(rownames, t, df, p, d, CI_lower, CI_upper)

# Study 2
df_baseline_study2 <- hr_long_study2 %>% group_by(id, game_length) %>% summarise(avg_explore = mean(chose_high_info_value))

a <- nice_t_test(data = df_baseline_study2, response = "avg_explore",mu = 0, warning = FALSE) 
b <- nice_t_test(data = subset(df_baseline_study2, game_length == 5), response = "avg_explore",mu = 0, warning = FALSE) 
c <- nice_t_test(data = subset(df_baseline_study2, game_length == 10), response = "avg_explore",mu = 0, warning = FALSE)
d <- nice_t_test(data = df_baseline_study2, response = "avg_explore", group = "game_length", alternative = "less", var.equal = TRUE) 

bind_rows(a, b, c, d) %>% cbind(rownames) %>% select(rownames, t, df, p, d, CI_lower, CI_upper)
```

### Orchard task (**main text results**)
```{r}
control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa",optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e6),check.nobs.vs.nRE = "ignore")

summary(lmer(exit_threshold ~ environment_type + (environment_type|id), data = tr_long, control = control))
```

# Is childhood unpredictability associated with reduced exploration?
### Horizon task
##### Directed exploration (**main text results**)
###### Study 1
In the model output below, check **unpredictability** for whether there is an effect of childhood unpredictability on directed exploration.
```{r}
mod1 <- lm(directed_exploration ~ unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + child_anxiety, data = hr_wide_study1)

summary(mod1)

tab_model(mod1)

(p1 <- plot_model(mod1, type="eff",
                  terms=c("unpredictability"), 
                  title = "Directed Exploration in Study 1", 
                  axis.title = c("Childhood Unpredictability (Standardized)", "% Exploration"),
                  show.data = TRUE, jitter= NULL, line.size = 1) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-1, 3.3), breaks = c(-1, 0, 1, 2, 3)) + ylim(0.1,0.75))
# ggsave(path = "../Plots/", filename = "directed_exploration_main.png", width = 15, height = 10, units = "cm")
```

###### Study 2
```{r}
mod2 <- lm(directed_exploration ~ unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + perceived_stress, data = hr_wide_study2)

summary(mod2)

tab_model(mod2)

(p2 <- plot_model(mod2, type="eff",
                  terms=c("unpredictability"), 
                  title = "Directed Exploration in Study 2", 
                  axis.title = c("Childhood Unpredictability (Standardized)", "% Exploration"),
                  show.data = TRUE, jitter= NULL, line.size = 1) + 
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-1, 4), breaks = c(-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4)) + ylim(0.1,0.75))
# ggsave(path = "../Plots/", filename = "directed_exploration_replication.png", width = 15, height = 10, units = "cm")
```

##### Strategic directed exploration (**main text results**)
```{r}
### Re-level factors to compare exploration in short and long horizon games
# set the reference level to long horizon games
hr_long_study1$horizon <- relevel(as.factor(hr_long_study1$horizon), ref = 1)
hr_long_study2$horizon <- relevel(as.factor(hr_long_study2$horizon), ref = 1)

# set the reference level to reward-information conflict games
hr_long_study1$conflict <- relevel(as.factor(hr_long_study1$conflict), ref = 1)
hr_long_study2$conflict <- relevel(as.factor(hr_long_study2$conflict), ref = 1)
```

###### Study 1
In the model output below, check **horizon:unpredictability** for whether there is an effect of childhood unpredictability on strategic exploration.
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa",optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e7))

mod3 <- glmer(chose_high_info_value ~ horizon*conflict*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + child_anxiety + (1 + horizon + conflict |id), data = hr_long_study1, family = binomial, control = control)

summary(mod3)

tab_model(mod3)

emtrends(mod3, pairwise ~ horizon, var="unpredictability")

# note: HEX color codes from https://projects.susielu.com/viz-palette
(p3 <- plot_model(mod3, type="eff",
                  terms=c("unpredictability", "horizon"), 
                  title = "Strategic directed exploration in Study 1", 
                  legend.title = "Horizon", 
                  axis.title = c("Childhood Unpredictability (Standardized)", "Pr(Exploration)"),
                  show.data = FALSE, jitter= NULL, line.size = 1) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = c("#D72C2C", "#0000FF"), 
                       labels = c("Short horizon", "Long horizon"), 
                       aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) + 
    # scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-1, 3.3), breaks = c(-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4)) + 
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.15, 0.70), breaks = c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6)))
#   ylim(0,0.70)) + 
# ylim(0.15,0.70))
# ggsave(path = "../Plots/", filename = "strategic_directed_exploration_main.png", width = 15, height = 10, units = "cm")
```

# What mechanisms underlie the relationship between childhood unpredictability and reduced exploration in the Horizon task?
### Candidate mechanism 1: Temporal discounting (**main text results**)
###### Study 1
In the model output below, check **conflict:unpredictability** for the effect of childhood unpredictability on temporal discounting. Note that the significant result goes against the hypothesis of temporal discounting. 
```{r}
control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa",optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e7))

mod8 <- glmer(chose_high_info_value ~ horizon*conflict*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + child_anxiety + (1 + horizon + conflict |id), data = hr_long_study1, family = binomial, control = control)

summary(mod8)

tab_model(mod8)

emtrends(mod8, pairwise ~ conflict, var="unpredictability")

(p5 <- plot_model(mod8, type="eff",
                  terms=c("unpredictability", "conflict"), 
                  title = "Temporal Discounting in Study 1", 
                  legend.title = "Reward-information Conflict", 
                  axis.title = c("Childhood Unpredictability (Standardized)", "Pr(Exploration)"),
                  show.data = FALSE, jitter= NULL, line.size = 1) +
    # scale_color_discrete(labels = c("Conflict games", "No conflict games"))  + 
    scale_color_manual(values = c("#D72C2C", "#0000FF"), 
                       labels = c("Conflict games", "No conflict games"), 
                       aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) + 
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.05,0.90), breaks = c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8)))
# ylim(0.05,0.85))
ggsave(path = "../Plots/", filename = "temporal_discounting_main.png", width = 15, height = 10, units = "cm")
```

### Candidate mechanism 2: Habitual responding (**main text results**)

##### Mediation Analysis
###### Study 1
Uncertainty-modulated habitual responding mediates childhood unpredictability and reduced directed exploration in the Horizon task. In the model output below, check **ab** under **Defined Parameters** for whether there is there is a mediation effect.  
```{r}
med1 <- ' # direct effect
             directed_exploration ~ c*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income
           # mediator
             habit_low_info_value ~ a*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income
             directed_exploration ~ b*habit_low_info_value
           # indirect effect (a*b)
             ab := a*b
           # total effect
             total := c + (a*b)
         '

fit <- sem(med1, data = hr_wide_study1)
summary(fit)
```

###### Study 2
```{r}
med2 <- ' # direct effect
             directed_exploration ~ c*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income
           # mediator
             habit_low_info_value ~ a*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income
             directed_exploration ~ b*habit_low_info_value
           # indirect effect (a*b)
             ab := a*b
           # total effect
             total := c + (a*b)
         '

fit <- sem(med2, data = hr_wide_study2)
summary(fit)
```
